section.title: Two Years, and After
section.form_description: Two old friends going back over the campaigns over beers. Warm, unhurried, no case to make — just "remember when." Sections are adventures recalled, and the narration keeps losing the thread onto opinions about lore, culture and how things work, then circling back. Runs everything against the Shepard it remembers — this persona's choices, temper and habits are the yardstick the stories and the digressions get measured by.
section.form_note: Two old friends over drinks, except the beer is on a cliff on Rannoch and the war is the Migrant Fleet's and the Council races' shared one. Tali and Liara alternate turns strictly, 6 each; no voice holds two in a row, since this is exactly the kind of unhurried back-and-forth the form wants. Each turn's first promise is its reply to the one before — Liara picks up Tali's line about the air, Tali corrects Liara's secondhand version of the trial, and so on — and both keep losing the thread onto lore (geth cognition, Thessia, admiralty politics, asari mourning custom) before drifting back to the cliff. The two women never knew Shepard chose Synthesis, and the section list is built so neither has to name it: they talk about what changed after the Crucible fired, not why.

required_facts.fact: After killing the yahg Shadow Broker on Hagalaz in 2185 and taking over his information network, Liara T'Soni ran the organization from the Broker's aging storm-riding ship, with the drell Feron and the renamed Info Drone "Glyph" assisting her. Only a handful of people, such as Admiral Hackett, knew the leadership had changed; on the black market, agents merely sensed the Shadow Broker had "gone soft." Sometime shortly before or during the opening of the 2186 Reaper invasion, Liara learned that the Illusive Man had tracked her down and intended to seize the Shadow Broker Base for Cerberus. Knowing the old ship could not survive spaceflight and expecting an assault, Liara and Feron loaded as much of the base's information drives and communications equipment as they could aboard a shuttle and escaped as Cerberus ships closed in. Liara then remotely piloted the abandoned base into a Cerberus cruiser, destroying both vessels. Liara relocated her operation to the renovated Normandy SR-2, setting up the Broker equipment in Miranda Lawson's former quarters and resuming her eavesdropping and resource-brokering in support of the war effort. Her network of agents remained largely intact, though the war steadily thinned their numbers, and some of the Broker's caches were left scattered across the galaxy awaiting recovery. Assorted technology salvaged from the wreck of the base was later contributed to the construction of the Crucible. Liara made no move to reveal her identity, and long-time underlings such as Barla Von never learned of the change; a surviving Urdnot Wrex might only make sly allusions to it.

scenes.title: Liara Hires Feron to Find Shepard
scenes.when: 2183, roughly two months after the Normandy SR-1 was destroyed, during Liara's search for Shepard
scenes.where: an ambush site, a Cerberus meeting with the Illusive Man, and the Afterlife Club on Omega

beats.text: Liara T'Soni hired the drell information trafficker Feron to help find Commander Shepard. He told her Shepard was neither dead nor alive; she insisted on searching anyway.
Blue Suns sent by the Shadow Broker ambushed the pair to delay Liara. An unknown sniper gunned the mercenaries down, opening a gap for the two to escape.

They ran into Cerberus agents, Miranda Lawson among them, and were brought before the Illusive Man, who revealed that the Shadow Broker was working with the Collectors. Afterward Feron admitted to Liara he had been ordered to lead her away from Shepard, but chose to help her instead.

At the Afterlife Club on Omega, Feron learned where the Blue Suns would bring Shepard's body and spotted the Broker's enforcer Tazzik. Rather than let Liara rush him, Feron tried a nearby turret on Tazzik's ship, missed, and Tazzik fled Omega with the body.
Liara accused Feron of still working for the Shadow Broker. He admitted he had never stopped — and said that connection was how they would track Tazzik.

scenes.title: Infiltrating the Shadow Broker's Base on Alingon
scenes.when: 2183, during Liara's search for Shepard's body, after Tazzik fled Omega
scenes.where: the Shadow Broker's main base on Alingon

beats.text: Feron's cramped ship reached Alingon, where the Broker's automated sentries opened fire; Feron threaded the ship through an asteroid field to shake them.

Inside, Feron passed Liara off as an asari escort on unscheduled Broker business to get past the outside guards, then led her toward the Broker's command center to find what the Broker was getting from the Collectors.

Liara addressed the Broker directly, rejecting the idea of Shepard's body as merchandise and arguing there was a link between the Reapers and the Collectors with Shepard at its center. She moved to attack and found she had been speaking to a holoprojector; the Broker said Tazzik had already completed the sale. Enraged, Liara biotically demolished the command center while Feron finished downloading the Broker's dealings onto a data stick.

Feron told Liara the body was still at the north portal. En route he came clean: Cerberus had recruited him, he and the Illusive Man had planned for Feron to snatch the body, and he had used Liara to do it. Alarms brought Broker security; Liara cut through them, including the two turian guards who had leered at her earlier, and took the data stick for safekeeping.

At the portal Feron broke cover to tell Tazzik and a Collector that the Broker wanted full payment for the body. Tazzik nearly believed him until the Collector blurted that Feron was a traitor. The distraction let Liara kill the guards and the Collector drone, but the body had already been reloaded onto Tazzik's ship.

Feron held Tazzik off so Liara could run; she was forced to leave him behind, captured. She delivered Shepard's body to Cerberus at Minuteman Station, put the Shadow Broker on her list of enemies, and vowed to free Feron.

evidence.page: The SSV Normandy SR-1 (Part 2) — Drive Core, Stealth, and Service History
evidence.text: **Summary:** Part 2 of a breakdown of the SSV Normandy SR-1: the Tantalus drive core, the Internal Emission Sink stealth system, the ship's extraordinary cost, its otherwise standard frigate armament and ~50-person crew, and its service history from the Eden Prime mission in 2183 through the Battle of the Citadel to its destruction over Alchera by the Collectors. Part 1 covers the ship's purpose and interior.

The SSV Normandy SR-1 (Systems Alliance Space Vehicle Normandy Stealth Reconnaissance-1) was a prototype "deep scout" frigate, first of the Normandy class, co-developed by the Systems Alliance and the Turian Hierarchy with Citadel Council sponsorship. Commissioned in 2183 and named for the 1944 Battle of Normandy, she was optimized for solo reconnaissance deep in unstable regions. She was initially commanded by Alliance officer Elli Zander, who was removed after clashing with turian chief engineer Octavio Tatum over the drive core's limits; David Anderson then took command, and shortly after handed the ship to Commander Shepard when Shepard became the first human Spectre.

The Normandy was built on three decks: a Command Deck with bridge, airlock, CIC and comm room; a habitation deck with quarters, mess, medical bay and captain's cabin; and an engineering and storage level holding the M35 Mako and the drive core. Her defining feature was the IES (internal emission sink) stealth system, which stored waste heat in lithium heat sinks, allowing silent running for hours; the system did not work at FTL and could be defeated by visual scan. It was powered by the experimental Tantalus Drive Core, roughly twice the size of a normal core and costing about 120 billion credits. Like all frigates she carried GARDIAN lasers, kinetic barriers, a spinal mass accelerator, and could mount Javelin disruptor torpedoes. Key crew included Joker (helmsman), Navigator Charles Pressly, Dr. Karin Chakwas, Engineer Greg Adams, Kaidan Alenko, Ashley Williams, and later Tali'Zorah nar Rayya, Garrus Vakarian and Urdnot Wrex.

During her shakedown the Normandy went to Eden Prime to recover a Prothean Beacon, which was destroyed during a geth attack. Rear Admiral Mikhailovich later inspected and criticized her as over-designed. When the Council refused to pursue Saren Arterius, Udina locked the ship down; with Anderson's help Shepard stole her and flew to Ilos. At the Battle of the Citadel the Normandy led the assault that destroyed Sovereign. In 2183 an unidentified starship (later revealed as a Collector cruiser) ambushed and destroyed the Normandy near Alchera, killing over twenty crew including Pressly; Shepard died saving Joker. Cerberus later built the larger Normandy SR-2 from the SR-1's design.

*For the ship featured in Mass Effect 2, see Normandy SR\-2.* The Normandy is shown patrolling the Omega Nebula for geth, near the planet Alchera. An unidentifiable starship suddenly appears and moves to intercept the Normandy, despite the frigate's stealth systems being active. Realizing that the ship is hostile, Joker initiates evasive maneuvers. The pursuing ship unleashes a barrage of beam weaponry that easily penetrates the Normandy's defenses. The Normandy's kinetic barriers and weapon systems are knocked out with a single hit. Within seconds, the Normandy is crippled as more hits breach the upper deck of the ship and destroy one of the starboard engine nacelles. The sudden attack claims the lives of over twenty crew members, Navigator Pressly among them. The order is given to abandon ship and the surviving crew evacuate the ship via escape pods. Commander Shepard stays behind to save Joker, who is still desperately trying to pilot the disintegrating ship. Shepard manages to place Joker in the last escape pod as their attacker makes a final pass on the Normandy, completely destroying the ship. While Joker's pod is successfully ejected, Shepard is knocked into space by the final explosion and drifts into the orbit of Alchera along with debris from the Normandy. Within the next two years, Commander Shepard's body is recovered and revived through the Lazarus Project by the pro\-human black ops organization Cerberus. They give Shepard command of a new ship similar in design to the Normandy SR\-1 but larger and bearing the insignia of Cerberus. Shepard and Joker decide to designate this new ship the Normandy SR\-2 in honor of the original Normandy. The new Normandy is nearly twice the size of the original, comprising five decks, compared to the SR\-1's three decks. If Shepard asks the ship's artificial intelligence how Cerberus managed to obtain the confidential schematics for the Normandy SR\-1 to build the SR\-2, it is revealed that Cerberus used their substantial influence to jump\-start the Alliance's decision to build the original SR\-1 in the first place, and subsequently obtain the secrets of advanced turian technology that the project required for themselves. Throughout the rest of 2185, Commander Shepard uses the new Normandy to scour the galaxy looking for the best biotics, scientists and warriors in an effort to build a team capable of taking on the Collectors and putting an end to their galaxy\-wide campaign of mass human abductions. At some point during this mission, the Alliance may locate the crash site of the original Normandy on Alchera, prompting Admiral Hackett to ask for Shepard's assistance in planting a memorial at the wreckage in honor of the lives lost in addition to recovering dog tags of the twenty missing crew members. If Shepard visits the site, they may experience several flashbacks of their time aboard the Normandy SR\-1, including of Pressly and the squad member that was left behind on Virmire. The Commander may even find their lost N7 helmet among the wreckage.

evidence.page: The SSV Normandy SR-2 (Part 1) — Origin and EDI
evidence.text:
Part 1 of a breakdown of the Normandy SR-2. The SR-1 was a prototype deep-scout stealth frigate co-developed by the Alliance and the Turian Hierarchy under Citadel Council sponsorship, commissioned in 2183. It was first commanded by an Alliance officer who clashed with the Turian chief engineer over the drive core's limits and was removed in favor of David Anderson, then passed to Commander Shepard when Shepard became the first human Spectre. About a month after the Battle of the Citadel, an unidentified starship intercepted the Normandy despite its active stealth systems. Joker began evasive maneuvers, but the attacker's beam weapons cut straight through the ship's defenses, knocking out kinetic barriers and weapons in a single hit. Within seconds the ship was crippled, the upper decks breached, a starboard drive cell destroyed, and over 20 crew killed, including Shepard. The SR-1 was completely destroyed above Alchera.

The Normandy SR-2 entered service in 2185 as the SR-1's successor. The Illusive Man had Cerberus build it at deliberately secret expense in the Voyager Cluster for the revived Shepard's team, to fight the Collectors' galaxy-wide human abductions; it served as headquarters of the Lazarus Cell. It was closely based on the SR-1's layout but almost twice the mass, with more crew-oriented comforts (civilian-grade accommodations, leather chairs, a kitchen). It kept the SR-1's stealth characteristics, but its greater mass meant it could not land on every planet, so shore parties used a shuttle. It carried over the SR-1's lithium-heat-sink stealth array and the oversized Tantalus drive core.

The SR-2's most significant upgrade was EDI, the Enhanced Defense Intelligence, an AI represented by a floating blue holographic sphere at terminals throughout the ship. EDI provided information about the Normandy and Cerberus and functioned as the ship's electronic-warfare defense. Because of the danger of a rogue AI, EDI was given behavioral blocks and could not interface with ship systems directly. When the Collectors boarded and abducted most of the crew, an emergency response by EDI and Joker released those blocks, granting EDI full control of the Normandy. Before the crew defected from Cerberus, EDI also served as the Illusive Man's eyes and ears aboard, monitoring listening devices and sending reports, while the Illusive Man restricted Shepard's access to some of EDI's files. EDI gained access to anti-Reaper algorithms and revealed she was designed in part with technology from Sovereign's remains, making her herself partly based on Reaper technology. After the defection, EDI, a fully sentient AI with free will, followed Shepard's lead and severed her ties to Cerberus, though she still downplayed her sentience to unfamiliar Alliance personnel.

Normandy Crash Site was a Mass Effect 2 assignment delivered as free Cerberus Network DLC. After acquiring the Normandy SR-2, Shepard received an e-mail from Admiral Hackett ("Normandy Crash Site Located") reporting that Alliance scans in the Amada System, Omega Nebula, had located the wreckage of the SSV Normandy on the planet Alchera. The Alliance asked Shepard to place a memorial monument on the site and to recover any sign of the 20 crew members still unaccounted for after the Collector attack that destroyed the ship.

The assignment was a solo exploration with no hostiles. As Shepard walked the frozen crash site, the Commander experienced flashbacks to areas of the SR-1: the ship docked at the Citadel in Dock 422, Joker at the cockpit controls, the sleeper pods, the Mako in the cargo bay, the CIC and Galaxy Map, Navigator Pressly saluting, and the squad member left behind on Virmire. Notable wreckage included the intact Mako, the destroyed Galaxy Map, port armor plating still reading "Normandy," the sleeper pod compartment, a cockpit section, and an upright escape pod.

Twenty dog tags were scattered across the map, most inside yellow crates, each belonging to a lost crew member (Bakari, Barrett, Chase, Crosby, the two Dravens, Dubyansky, Emerson, Felawa, Gladstone, Grenado, Grieco, Laflamme, Lowe, Negulesco, Pakti, Rahman, Tanaka, Tucks, Waaberi). A datapad belonging to Navigator Pressly held three journal entries charting his shift from distrust of the ship's alien crew to a declaration that he would die for any member of the crew regardless of their birthworld. Shepard's lost N7 helmet could also be recovered; if found it appeared on the desk in the Commander's SR-2 quarters. Four containers held 500 units of element zero total.

Shepard had to place the monument to complete the assignment; returning to the shuttle afterward ended the mission. If at least one dog tag was recovered, Hackett sent a follow-up e-mail thanking Shepard on behalf of the notified families. Rewards included 3,750 credits in Alliance funding, 500 element zero, and up to 240 experience. In Mass Effect 3, the names of all crew lost with the SR-1 appear on the Normandy SR-2's memorial wall regardless of how many dog tags were collected.

**Alchera** is the *fourth* planet orbiting the star Amada. *Main article: Alchera* - *Assignment:* Normandy Crash Site (assignment)

The Normandy SR\-2 first enters service in 2185, and serves as the "successor" to the SR\-1\. The Illusive Man had Cerberus build the SR\-2 for the newly\-revived Commander Shepard's team to aid them in their mission to stop the Collectors' galaxy\-wide campaign of human abductions. The ship serves as the headquarters of the Lazarus Cell. Constructed at great and laborious expense in the Voyager Cluster, the ship is very similar to the Systems Alliance's SSV Normandy SR\-1, having been based on the design layout of the original. The Normandy SR\-2 has several key differences, the most significant being that she is almost twice the mass of the original. Cerberus also designed the ship with more crew\-oriented comforts by including civilian\-grade accommodations (like leather chairs and a kitchen). The ship still retains the SSV Normandy SR\-1's stealth characteristics. However, unlike the SR\-1, the SR\-2 cannot land on every planet—due to her increased mass—requiring shore parties to use a shuttle to get to a planet's surface.

Lieutenant Gregory Adams was a human Systems Alliance engineer of the 22nd century, hand-picked by Captain David Anderson to serve as Chief Engineer of the SSV Normandy. He had served on every class of Alliance starship, most recently the SSV Tokyo, which he considered a good ship but inferior to the Normandy. Aboard the Normandy SR-1 he maintained a friendship with Navigator Pressly, remained calm and even-tempered, and could brief Commander Shepard on the ship's IES stealth system and engines. He expressed condolences after Corporal Jenkins died on Eden Prime, welcomed non-human crew, was impressed by Tali'Zorah nar Rayya's technical skill and took her under his wing, and was untroubled when Shepard took the Normandy to the Terminus Systems.

After the SR-1 was destroyed, Adams and most surviving crew were reassigned. Unlike Dr. Chakwas and Joker, he declined to join the Cerberus-backed Normandy SR-2 in 2185, citing prior run-ins with Cerberus and disbelief that Shepard was alive; Tali noted his absence was hard to get used to.

In Mass Effect 3, Adams returned to lead the SR-2 engine room after the ship was turned over to the Alliance. He was the first to recognize EDI as an AI rather than a VI. He apologized to Shepard for refusing the earlier call and later discussed his regret with Chakwas or Dr. Michel in the crew quarters. When EDI went offline after the Palaven mission, Adams brought a fire extinguisher to the AI Core and helped as EDI took over Eva Coré's body. If Mordin was absent, Adams contacted EDI about the IFF upgrade and its evolving encryption keys. He offered Shepard a GX12 thermal pipe to make the drive core safer; installing it also let Daniels and Donnelly develop eezo capacitor improvements usable on the Crucible. A firm proponent of synthetic life as valid sapient life, Adams debated the topic with Donnelly and the ship's doctor, with Shepard able to weigh in. After Thessia he could be found with Kaidan praising Liara's resilience. Before the final battle he told Shepard the Normandy was ready and closed with, "It has been an honor and privilege to serve with you." Roger Jackson voiced Adams, who also voices Harkin.

Sometime after the destruction of the SSV Normandy, Aria is approached by Liara T'Soni and Feron while looking for Commander Shepard's body. Feron tells Liara to let him do the talking, which leads to Aria teasing her for being unable to speak. Aria says that she would divulge where the Blue Suns were taking the body if they tell her why the Shadow Broker is so interested. Liara then blurts out that the Shadow Broker is selling the body to the Collectors, catching Aria off guard. Refusing to show weakness, she tells Liara and Feron to leave, but not before disclosing the trade off location. |  | ***“I have so many questions.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect: Discovery** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

evidence.text:
Feron was a drell information trafficker who described himself as "an information trader. Not a slaver." In Mass Effect: Redemption, set after the destruction of the Normandy SR-1, Liara T'Soni hired him to help find Commander Shepard; he reported that Shepard was neither dead nor alive. Ambushed by Blue Suns sent by the Shadow Broker to delay Liara, the pair were saved by an unknown sniper, then encountered Cerberus agents, including Miranda Lawson, and were brought to the Illusive Man, who revealed the Shadow Broker was working with the Collectors. Feron admitted he had been ordered to lead Liara away from Shepard but chose to help her instead.

Feron took Liara to Afterlife on Omega, where Aria T'Loak resided, and learned where the Blue Suns would bring Shepard's body. He spotted the Broker's enforcer Tazzik but missed his ship with a turret, letting Tazzik flee Omega with the body. Feron revealed he had never stopped working for the Shadow Broker, which they could exploit to track Tazzik. The two infiltrated the Broker's base on Alingon, with Feron passing Liara off as his prisoner; he downloaded the Broker's dealings while Liara distracted a hologram of the Broker. Feron confessed Cerberus had recruited him and that he and the Illusive Man had planned for Feron to snatch the body. When a Collector exposed him as a traitor, Feron held off Tazzik so Liara could escape, and was captured.

In Mass Effect 2, Liara mentioned a "friend" lost during her search. During Lair of the Shadow Broker, Liara, Shepard, and Cerberus intel led to the Shadow Broker Base on Hagalaz, where Feron was found being tortured on a device that could not be removed without killing him. Liara and Shepard killed the Shadow Broker; Liara took over the role, and Feron chose to stay and assist her, mentally scarred and using his drell memory recall to survive the torture. In Mass Effect 3, if Shepard helped Liara take the Broker ship, Feron helped evacuate it during a Cerberus attack, became one of Liara's agents controlling Terminus operations (to Tazzik's dismay), and emailed Shepard offering information via Glyph. If Shepard did not help overthrow the Broker, Liara hired mercenaries to storm the lair and Feron did not survive.

evidence.text: Liara single\-handedly defeats a squad of the Shadow Broker's guards. Feron catches up with her, but Liara shrugs him off, angry that he lied and has been a triple agent all along: his employer is Cerberus. He explains that he started out working for the Shadow Broker running small errands. Cerberus had been trying to recruit him repeatedly to gain a foothold in the Broker's operation. Feron only gave in to Cerberus when he learned that the Broker was working with the Collectors, and that the Collectors were interested in Commander Shepard's corpse. The Broker had become suspicious however, and was cutting Feron out of work. To get back in, Feron volunteered to steer Liara away from finding Shepard so he could retrieve Shepard himself. Feron also let Tazzik escape Omega so he had an excuse to return to Alingon and grab as much information about the Shadow Broker's dealings as he could. At the Alingon base's hangar, Liara and Feron watch as the Collector they saw earlier examines Shepard's body. Tazzik is ready to hand it over as soon as the Broker receives the promised payment. Feron boldly interrupts the scene, telling Tazzik that the Broker is unsatisfied with the current deal and wants all of the Collectors' payment now, before the body is exchanged. Tazzik believes him, and orders the body moved back into his ship's hold. Elsewhere, the Collector fumes to the Shadow Broker about this "betrayal". The Broker explains that Feron does not speak for him and is a traitor, but he can't communicate with Tazzik. Back in the hangar, the Collector alerts Tazzik, who pulls a gun on Feron. Liara hears Feron's signal and attacks the other guards and the Collector while Feron holds off Tazzik. Liara escapes on Tazzik's ship, but is forced to leave Feron behind. Sometime later at a Cerberus facility, Miranda and Liara watch as Cerberus doctors work on Commander Shepard's body. Liara suggests that bringing Shepard back may not be the right thing to do. Miranda expresses doubts that Shepard can be revived because the body was in worse condition than expected and the stasis container was of little help, but says the Illusive Man is more optimistic and willing to devote a considerable amount of resources toward the project. Liara leaves, realizing she has another friend to help now, and another enemy.

evidence.text: Feron is hired by Liara T'Soni to help her find Commander Shepard. However, he tells her that the Commander is neither dead nor alive. Nonetheless, Liara insists on finding Shepard. Unfortunately, they are ambushed by the Blue Suns, sent by the Shadow Broker to delay Liara. Suddenly, an unknown sniper guns down the mercenaries, giving the two an opening to escape. They then run into agents of Cerberus, a pro\-human extremist group, who claim that they are after Shepard too. Among the Cerberus agents is Miranda Lawson. The pair is brought to meet with the Illusive Man who reveals the Shadow Broker is working with the Collectors. After the meeting, Feron reveals to Liara that he has been ordered to lead her away from Shepard. But because of recent events, he is willing to help her. Feron brings Liara back to the Afterlife Club, where the queen of Omega, Aria T'Loak resides. After learning the location where the Blue Suns would be bringing the body, Feron spots Tazzik, the Broker's personal enforcer. Liara is half of mind to simply rush, but Feron thinks of a better idea with a nearby turret. Unfortunately, he misses Tazzik's ship, alerting the Suns to their presence. Tazzik is then able to flee Omega, with Shepard's body. Liara accuses Feron of still working for the Shadow Broker. The two infiltrate the Broker's main base on Alingon, where Feron passes off Liara as his prisoner. Upon entry, they see what seems to be a shadowy hologram of the Broker. Liara keeps him talking while Feron downloads all of the information on the Broker's dealings. As soon as he is finished, he tells Liara to unleash her biotics to disable the communications in the room, preventing any of the Broker's hired guns from learning their location. While en route to Shepard's location, Feron admits to Liara that Cerberus attempted to recruit him a few times but he refused to betray the Broker, until hearing about his deal with the Collectors. Working directly with the Illusive Man, they came up with a plan for Feron himself to snatch the body. But the Broker learned about this, so Feron had to use Liara to accomplish the plan. Feron then meets Tazzik and the Collector he is talking with, claiming that the Broker wanted full payment for Shepard's body. Tazzik is willing to believe him, until the Collector blurts out that Feron's a traitor. The drell holds off Tazzik so that Liara can escape. Miranda gives Liara the location of a Cerberus rendezvous point where she can bring Shepard's body once she has it, and tells Liara to follow Feron before departing. evidence.text:
The Shadow Broker was an enigmatic figure at the head of a vast organization that traded in information, always selling to the highest bidder. The Broker balanced its sales so that no client ever gained a decisive advantage, forcing customers to keep trading and keeping the organization in business. The Broker operated only through agents, and its identity was unknown to the public. In 2183 Barla Von called the Broker "he" for convenience but believed it was a group, since no single individual could monitor so much information.

The Broker's dealings touched many events. In 2161 it tasked its associate Brooks to kill Roth, a Cerberus funder, and transfer his funds to Barla Von; Brooks was shot and left for dead, derailing the plan. The Broker also arranged the conspicuous destruction of the turian frigate Verrikan to embarrass the Hierarchy, hiring Zaeed Massani for the job. Tali'Zorah came to the Citadel to trade her evidence that Saren Arterius had gone rogue, routed through the Broker's agent Fist, but Fist had switched allegiance to Saren, so the furious Broker hired Urdnot Wrex to kill him. Admiral Kahoku bought the Broker's services to locate Cerberus, learning only that they were active in the Voyager Cluster. Batarian mercenaries once used the Broker to learn Thane Krios's identity, leading to the murder of his wife Irikah.

After the Normandy SR-1's destruction, the Collectors hired the Broker to retrieve Shepard's body; the Broker sent its enforcer Tazzik, who succeeded despite interference from Liara T'Soni and Feron. Liara and Feron tracked Tazzik to the Broker's base on Alingon, where they found the Broker was communicating through a machine; Feron was captured. Pursuing Feron, Liara eventually teamed with Commander Shepard to raid the Broker's ship on Hagalaz. The Shadow Broker was revealed to be a yahg, a pre-spaceflight species from Parnack; the original Broker had had a yahg abducted for study around 2125, and the captive, operating as "Operative Kechlu," killed and replaced his handler, then pre-empted the Broker's attempt to eliminate him and seized the role, running the organization for about six decades. Having learned of the Reapers and the truth about the Collectors, he had dealt with the Collectors in a bid for his own survival. Shepard and Liara killed the yahg by turning his own kinetic technology against him, and Liara became the new Shadow Broker, taking his Info Drone (renamed "Glyph"). In 2186, facing a Cerberus takeover attempt, Liara crashed the Broker's ship into a Cerberus cruiser and relocated operations aboard the Normandy SR-2. Few knew of the leadership change; the black market only sensed the Broker had "gone soft." An audio log revealed Alec Ryder had reached the Broker through Barla Von for help developing SAM. The Broker's troops wore black-and-white armor bearing a triangular red emblem resembling a yahg's maw, and its forces included Agents, Engineers, Heavies, Vanguards, and Rocket Drones.

evidence.text:
Lair of the Shadow Broker was a Mass Effect 2 mission in which Commander Shepard helped Liara T'Soni track down the Shadow Broker. It became available after the DLC install and the Horizon mission, triggered by a Cerberus message on the Galaxy Map titled "Give Liara Intel," offering intel on the Broker's base because of his past work for the Collectors. The mission ran without a break from Illium to its end and featured mostly shielded enemies.

On Illium, Shepard delivered the intel to Liara in her office; the data also revealed that Feron, Liara's drell partner who sacrificed himself two years earlier, was still alive. Arriving at Liara's apartment, Shepard met the asari Spectre Tela Vasir investigating an assassination attempt on Liara. Clues led to Sekat, an information broker at the Dracon Trade Center, which exploded as the squad arrived. Fighting through the Shadow Broker's private army with Vasir, Shepard found Liara alive; Liara exposed Vasir as a long-time Shadow Broker asset who had killed Sekat and taken his data. Vasir fled, leading to a firefight, a skycar chase through Nos Astra, and a rooftop battle at the Azure hotel that ended with Shepard killing Vasir, who justified her betrayal as the price of intel that saved lives and accused Shepard of hypocrisy for working with Cerberus.

The trail led to the Broker's ship orbiting in the perpetual storm band of Hagalaz. Shepard, with Liara as a mandatory squadmate, fought across the ship's exterior amid lightning capacitors and maintenance drones, defended a door during a long five-wave siege, and pushed inside to free Feron. Confronting the Shadow Broker revealed him to be a yahg, taken from his homeworld and having killed and replaced the original Broker decades earlier. After a three-stage boss fight, Liara dropped an electrified fluid tank to overload his barrier and kill him. Liara assumed the Broker's identity and network, becoming the new Shadow Broker, and granted Shepard permanent access to the base. If Shepard had romanced Liara in Mass Effect, she later returned Shepard's dog tags recovered from the Normandy wreck. Rewards included 90,000 credits, element zero and palladium, and Heavy Pistol Damage and Damage Protection upgrades. Cut content included early plans to rescue Liara from the Broker or to make Shepard the Shadow Broker.

I didn't call.” After the SSV Normandy's destruction, the Shadow Broker is hired by the Collectors to retrieve Shepard's body and deliver it to them. As the Collector General is talking about the deal to the Shadow Broker, only one voice is responding to the Collector, further hinting that the Shadow Broker is indeed a singular individual. He sends Tazzik, his personal enforcer, to retrieve Shepard's remains from the Blue Suns on Omega, a task at which he succeeds despite interference from Liara T'Soni and Feron. When the two follow Tazzik to the Broker's base on Alingon, they come face\-to\-face with the Broker, so to speak, as an obscure shadowy figure. Liara talks to him while Feron downloads all the information on the Broker's dealings with the Collectors. When asked why he would sell Shepard to the Collectors, who may be working for the Reapers, the Broker answers that it is simply business. He doesn't believe that the Collectors could gain anything from a corpse. When Liara gets close enough to take a good look at the Broker, she finds that it is just a machine he's communicating through. But before the Broker could alert his men to their presence, Feron had finished downloading and Liara unleashes a powerful display of biotics, disabling the communications in the room. While the transaction for Shepard's corpse continues on the base, Liara and Feron attempt to fool Tazzik and the Collector intermediary into thinking the Broker is unhappy with the payment and is terminating the arrangement. The Collector General accuses the Broker of treachery through a direct line. The Broker assures the Collector that Feron doesn't speak for him, reporting the loss of his link to Alingon. Despite the General exposing Feron's duplicity through the intermediary, Liara is able to escape with Shepard's body, but is forced to leave Feron behind. |  | ***“The chances of surviving are… slim.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 2** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

evidence.text: Briefly daydreaming about the destruction of the SSV Normandy, Liara is woken by Miranda before being dropped off on the streets to resume the search. Based on Cerberus' reactions to Feron, Liara deduces that he is actually an agent for the Shadow Broker. Realizing she needed a guide to Omega but angry enough to biotically smack Feron in the face, Liara eventually cools off to resume working with him. Back again at Afterlife, Liara follows Feron's lead for a meeting with the pirate queen Aria T'Loak. Sexually harassed by a fat batarian and mistaken for "merchandise" by an enterprising volus, she promptly hands them their asses before Aria's henchman Anto clears them to see his boss. Feron does all the inquiries, but he is reluctant to answer Aria's query about the Broker's interest in Shepard. Liara speaks up that the Broker is actually in collusion with the Collectors, greatly angering Aria enough to have them thrown out. Liara demands recompense for her information, so Aria gives them the location where the Blue Suns are to hand over Shepard's body to the Shadow Broker. Liara and Feron covertly watch the transaction unfold at an old mining processing plant, but Liara springs to action as soon as she hears confirmation of the body as Shepard's. Feron barely prevents her from doing something rash, suggesting that he use a nearby turret to disable the Broker agent Tazzik's ship while Liara takes the meeting by surprise. However, Feron's shot misses the ship, losing Liara's stealth advantage and devolving the transaction into a melee. Despite Liara neutralizing the Blue Suns present, Tazzik manages to flee Omega with Shepard's corpse.

Lair of the Shadow Broker was a DLC pack for Mass Effect 2, announced on July 22, 2010 and released September 7 for Xbox 360 and PC, with technical issues preventing its sale in parts of Central and Eastern Europe. It concerned Liara T'Soni and her history with the Shadow Broker, and associate producer Michael Gamble described it as the "biggest DLC yet, period." It was the first piece of DLC to begin expanding the story in preparation for Mass Effect 3, and though playable during or after the suicide mission, its dialogue assumed the player had already completed that mission.

In the story Liara tracked down the mysterious Shadow Broker to recover a man he had kidnapped, chasing clues from Illium to the Broker's secret lair while his agents tried to stop her. The pack added one mission (Lair of the Shadow Broker), one location (the Shadow Broker Base in the Sowilo system of the Hourglass Nebula), the bonus power Stasis, six weapon and defense upgrades, the Shadow Broker intel center with new research, five achievements, two cabin items (Shepard's old dog tags and a Shadow Broker Base ship model), and the chance to continue a relationship with Liara.

It cost $9.99 USD on Xbox 360 or 800 BioWare Points on PC, was included on the disc of the PlayStation 3 version of Mass Effect 2, and was bundled into Mass Effect Legendary Edition. Pre-development notes mention cut plans including a player upgrade slowing time when injured, two tech upgrades for a "popular henchman," biotic and tech cooldown upgrades, and an intended runtime of about 2.5 hours.

evidence.text:
Shepard Wakes on the Lazarus Station. 2185, the Lazarus Project's final stage, during the mech sabotage the Lazarus Research Station — a Cerberus deep-space station: the medical bay, the corridors and docking area, the shuttle-bay door, then the escape shuttle

evidence.page: Miranda Briefs Rasa on the Lazarus Project
evidence.text: Miranda Briefs Rasa on the Lazarus Project. before the Reaper war, Minuteman Station (Mass Effect: Foundation 8), after the failed attempt to capture Jack the Lazarus Project labs and Miranda's office aboard Minuteman Station In the labs Miranda walks Rasa through the Lazarus Project: Shepard's backup clone in its tank, Shepard's own body mid-reconstruction on the operating table, and screens of everything Cerberus holds on Shepard. She tells Rasa not to worry about Leng — muscle has its uses, but information is more powerful, and Rasa's intelligence has been invaluable to the project. The clone, though, is not what the Illusive Man wants; he wants the real Shepard, known down to the smallest detail.

The Lazarus Project was a Cerberus project whose sole purpose was to bring Commander Shepard back from the dead. After Shepard was killed in a Collector attack that destroyed the SSV Normandy, Cerberus recovered Shepard's corpse with the help of Liara T'Soni. The Illusive Man created and funded the project, pouring in vast resources in the belief that only Shepard could stop the Reaper threat while the Council did nothing.

The project took two years and over 4 billion credits, undertaken by the Lazarus Cell headed by Miranda Lawson with her assistant Wilson. It involved cybernetic implants to reconstruct Shepard's skeleton, rebuilding of skin, and fluids to restart blood flow and organs, along with facial reconstruction; Shepard partially lost prior abilities and talents. The Illusive Man refused to implant a control chip in Shepard's brain, fearing it would alter Shepard's personality. The project succeeded in 2185 when Shepard regained full neurological activity.

Cerberus also created a clone of Shepard, kept secret and intended as a source of spare organs during the revival, though it was never used. In 2186 the disillusioned ex-Cerberus operative Maya Brooks awakened the clone and convinced it to kill and replace the original Shepard to pursue a pro-human agenda; Shepard stopped the clone from escaping the Citadel aboard the Normandy SR-2, and the clone was killed while Brooks was captured or killed. During the assault on Cronos Station near the end of the Reaper War, recovered Lazarus Project records confirmed Lawson's claim that Shepard had been reconstructed without genetic or neural tampering. The project's name references Lazarus of Bethany, raised from the dead in the Bible.

evidence.text: The Third Meeting, and the End of Kai Leng. 2186, Priority: Cerberus Headquarters, the assault on Cronos Station — the point of no return the Illusive Man's inner sanctum aboard Cronos Station, orbiting Anadius in the Horse Head Nebula The team fought through the hangar bay — stopping Cerberus from venting it into space — and the rotation and drive sections toward the Illusive Man's sanctum, passing video terminals that laid out the Lazarus Project that rebuilt Shepard, EDI's own origin as the Rogue VI, Kai Leng, and Cerberus's Reaper-implant research. A love interest in the squad had personal things to say at the Lazarus Project console.

- **Enhanced Defense Initiative** \- An initiative to create a "shackled" AI developed from a rogue Alliance VI and systems salvaged from Sovereign. The result was the Enhanced Defense Intelligence, or "EDI", which was installed onto the Normandy SR\-2 as an analysis and cyber warfare system. - **Lazarus Project** \- Established in 2183\. Based out of Lazarus Research Station and led by Miranda Lawson, the Lazarus Project spent billions of credits in pursuit of one goal: bringing Commander Shepard back to life. - **Project Doorway** \- Established in 2163\. Produced forged Council\-standard medicards and identitags to allow operatives unrestricted movement. - **Project Eva** \- Commissioned by the Illusive Man after Cerberus lost contact with Commander Shepard, EDI and the Normandy SR\-2 following the defeat of the Collectors. Project Eva developed Dr. Eva Coré, an infiltration mech. - **Project Firewalker** \- Responsible for field\-testing the prototype M\-44 Hammerhead planet\-side exploration rover. - **Project Mia** \- Developed by Cerberus scientists studying indoctrination and Reaper\-Husk communication who later fled the organization and took refuge on Gellix with their research. Due to the compartmentalization of the project's components, and at least one of the researchers is dead before the group's exodus, the surviving researchers could not piece together the true nature of the project. - **Project Overlord** \- Based on Aite, Overlord was intended to develop a specialized hybrid\-VI capable of controlling the geth to serve Cerberus. - **Project Phoenix** \- Experimented on enhancing human physiology to develop stronger biotics. Many Phoenix Operatives defected from Cerberus after the Illusive Man began using indoctrination to ensure the loyalty of his troops. Dragoons may have been the end\-result of Project Phoenix. - **Project Trapdoor** \- Established in 2168\. Using the front corporation New Dawn Pharmaceuticals, the drug omega\-enkaphalin (O\-E) was developed to disrupt the powers of biotics. Cerberus personnel were nanosurgically altered to resist O\-E. - **Unnamed Biotics Project** \- Based at Pragia's Teltin Facility, this project aimed to increase biotic potential in humans through experiments on child biotics kidnapped by Cerberus or bought from batarian slavers. Among the subjects were Jack and Aresh Aghdashloo. The project's highly unethical methods included the use of torture (both physical and psychological) and drugs on subjects as well as gladiatorial combat between subjects. Fatalities were not uncommon. The project ended following a riot by the child subjects, leading to the deaths of many guards and children. - **Unnamed Genetics Project** \- An illegal operation that aimed to create an unstoppable army. Its main base of operations is on the planet Nepheron. - **Unnamed** **Project** \- An operation to create a device that disrupts higher mental functions, allowing the victim to be controlled. Shut down sometime after Lazarus Project started. Finally used in the Andromeda Galaxy by a team of ex\-Cerberus scientists.

This is the second mission of the prologue. It begins right after completing Prologue: Save Joker, and it serves a dual purpose, providing a basic combat tutorial and introducing field mission concepts. This mission situates Commander Shepard in the Mass Effect 2 universe as a Cerberus operative with a new team. After the destruction of the Normandy SR\-1 and death of Commander Shepard two years earlier, Shepard's body was recovered by Cerberus, who spent the time rebuilding Shepard into a cybernetically\-enhanced symbol of humanity. After the opening credits, which show Shepard literally being rebuilt by the Lazarus Project, and a brief interlude showing Shepard regaining consciousness prematurely, the Commander awakens for the second time on an operating table at the Lazarus Research Station to alarm bells ringing, as the station's personnel come under attack from their own security mechs. Although alone and under\-equipped, Shepard is guided by an authoritative female voice over the intercom, the voice belonging to the woman looming over Shepard when they awoke the first time, eventually revealed to be Miranda Lawson, head of the Lazarus Project and commanding officer of the facility.

Prologue: Awakening was the second mission of Mass Effect 2, acquired automatically after Prologue: Save Joker. It served as a combat tutorial and established Commander Shepard as a Cerberus operative two years after the destruction of the Normandy SR-1 and Shepard's death. Shepard's body had been recovered by Cerberus and rebuilt through the Lazarus Project into a cybernetically enhanced operative. The opening credits showed the reconstruction; Shepard then woke prematurely once, then again on an operating table at the Lazarus Research Station as alarm bells rang and the station's own security mechs turned hostile.

Under-equipped and alone, Shepard was guided by radio by an authoritative woman later revealed as Miranda Lawson, head of the Lazarus Project and the station's commanding officer. Shepard collected a pistol, armor and thermal clips and fought through waves of Hacked Mechs, picking up an M-3 Predator Heavy Pistol and an M-100 Grenade Launcher along the way. Scattered laptops and datapads held audio and video logs from Miranda and Dr. Wilson describing the effort to revive Shepard, including that Shepard was returned without mental tampering. Wall safes and datapads could be bypassed or hacked for credits.

Shepard met Jacob Taylor on a bridge fighting mechs; Jacob confirmed he was on Shepard's side, revealed he was a biotic, and later disclosed that the Lazarus Project was a Cerberus operation, with morality points awarded for dialogue choices. Shepard then reached Dr. Wilson, who appeared wounded in the leg and was healed with medi-gel before joining temporarily. At the shuttle bay door, Miranda was waiting on the other side and shot Wilson dead without ceremony, explaining that he was the traitor who had hacked the security mechs, endangered the project, and caused the deaths of most of the staff.

During the shuttle ride to another Cerberus facility, Miranda questioned Shepard about pre-service history, psychological profile, and the squadmate lost on Virmire to assess memory. At the facility Shepard spoke with the Illusive Man by hologram, who explained that entire human colonies and thousands of colonists had vanished and tasked Shepard with investigating Freedom's Progress alongside Miranda and Jacob. The Lazarus Station was afterward destroyed by remote detonation to erase incriminating data. Shepard gained Jacob and Miranda as squad members and the mission awarded roughly 1,000 experience and 7,500 credits.

|  | ***“The chances of surviving are… slim.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 2** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- | The **Lazarus Cell** is one of the many cells operating within Cerberus. Like all Cerberus cells its members have no knowledge of their counterpart cells: a tactic that prevents captured Cerberus agents from compromising the security of other cells. The leading operative of the Lazarus Cell is Miranda Lawson, who reports to the Illusive Man. After Commander Shepard's death, the Lazarus Cell was tasked with the recovery and reanimation of Shepard's remains in what was known as the Lazarus Project. The cell labored aboard the Lazarus Research Station for two years and successfully revived Shepard. However, in the final stages of the project Wilson, the cell's medical officer, hacked and reprogrammed the station's mechs to attack its staff. Most of the cell's personnel were killed: only Miranda Lawson, her executive officer, Jacob Taylor, and the prematurely awakened Shepard survived. The survivors fled the station, which was subsequently destroyed by remote detonation. The surviving members of the Lazarus Cell traveled to Minuteman Station. There, the Illusive Man put Shepard in charge of the cell's activities and tasked the cell with discovering who or what caused the disappearance of tens of thousands of human colonists in the Terminus Systems. The cell's next mission was the investigation of Freedom's Progress: a human colony whose inhabitants had recently and mysteriously disappeared. The mission successfully confirmed that the Collectors were responsible for abducting colonists and the Illusive Man tasked the cell with stopping them. After the mission to Freedom's Progress, the cell's headquarters was moved to the recently completed Normandy SR\-2 and the cell was restaffed with 24 new members (according to EDI). Though under Shepard's command, Lawson retained her position as the cell's leading operative and continued sending reports to the Illusive Man. Shepard, Doctor Chakwas, Joker and the specialists that Shepard recruits for the mission are not official members of the Lazarus Cell or members of Cerberus. The fate of the Lazarus Cell depends on the player's choices in Mass Effect 2. Endings range from the Collectors destroying most of the cell's personnel (possibly including Shepard and the entire team) to Shepard saving the lives of his or her entire crew. If Shepard survives, he or she, as the leader of the cell, may cut ties with Cerberus or remain on good terms with the Illusive Man. In all cases the Lazarus Cell accomplishes its mission to stop the Collectors.

She hands Rasa a disc of highly classified but outdated Cerberus secrets to trade to the Spectre Tela Vasir for access. Vasir can get her inside; extracting the files is up to Rasa.

In her correspondence with the Illusive Man, Miranda reports Rasa's dangerous levels of savvy and knowledge about the Lazarus Project. She receives the advice to cut Cerberus losses if Rasa becomes a liability.

The Lazarus Research Station was a deep-space station used by Cerberus as headquarters for the Lazarus Cell and as the site of the Lazarus Project, the effort to revive Commander Shepard. Along with Minuteman Station, it was one of two facilities that housed and operated on Shepard's body and clone.

In Mass Effect: Foundation, the station's systems were breached in 2184 during a successful operation by the agent Rasa to steal Shepard's clone, with mechs, security feeds and sprinkler systems all affected. In Mass Effect 2, in 2185, the station suffered a catastrophic security breakdown when LOKI and YMIR mechs, allegedly reprogrammed by Wilson, turned on the personnel. During the crisis Shepard revived and escaped by shuttle with Miranda Lawson, the station's commanding officer, and Jacob Taylor, her executive officer, in the mission Prologue: Awakening. A later Illusive Man report revealed the station was destroyed by remote detonation, with a Cerberus team dispatched to ensure no incriminating evidence survived.

Miranda Lawson was a human Cerberus officer, born in 2150. She had no mother; her influential, wealthy, egomaniacal father genetically engineered her from a modified copy of his own genome to be a specimen of human perfection, with enhanced intelligence, strength, reflexes, biotics, looks, faster healing and an extended lifespan. She was the first "daughter" he kept. Denied friends and affection and pressured to always be better, she fled home, and her father pursued her across the galaxy until she joined Cerberus in exchange for protection, at which point he severed his ties to the group. She rose to answer directly to the Illusive Man.

In Mass Effect Galaxy she worked as an informant for Jacob Taylor, helping him foil a batarian plot to assassinate the Citadel Council with a bioweapon. In the Mass Effect: Foundation comics she recruited Jacob to Cerberus while searching Terminus space for the fallen Shepard's body, ran the Lazarus Project at Minuteman/Lazarus Station, used the agent Rasa to steal Shepard's Spectre files, and later pursued Rasa when she defected with Shepard's backup clone. In Mass Effect: Redemption she guided Liara and Feron toward recovering Shepard's body from the Shadow Broker's agents and had it transferred to Lazarus Research Station.

The Illusive Man placed Miranda in charge of the Lazarus Project, which spent two years and vast Cerberus resources reviving Shepard. She became Shepard's second-in-command aboard the Normandy SR-2 and a proxy for the Illusive Man, having wanted (but been denied) to implant Shepard with a control chip. Her loyalty mission, "Miranda: The Prodigal," concerned protecting her twin sister Oriana from their father. During the Suicide Mission she could lead the second fireteam, and if present when Shepard destroyed the Collector Base she resigned from Cerberus. She was a romance option for a male Shepard.

In Mass Effect 3, if she survived, Miranda spent the war investigating Oriana's disappearance. Her father Henry Lawson, allied with the Illusive Man, had abducted Oriana and taken her to the Sanctuary facility on Horizon, whose true purpose was processing refugees into Reaper husks. Miranda was gravely wounded by Kai Leng there. Whether she survived the Horizon confrontation depended on securing her loyalty, warning her about Kai Leng, and granting her Alliance resources; if she lived she killed Henry, planted a tracker on Kai Leng leading to Cronos Station, joined the war effort striking Cerberus targets, and reunited with Oriana. She could appear in Mass Effect 3: Citadel, including at Shepard's party where she sparred with Jack.

#### Deck 3: Crew Deck Deck 3 is the Crew Deck. It contains the medical bay, crew sleeping quarters, kitchen, observation decks, AI core, life support, bathrooms, Liara T'Soni's office and the main battery. Liara's office, located in the same space where Miranda's office/quarters was located in Mass Effect 2, contains the Broker Terminal, which gives you information about the characters Shepard can encounter during the fight, and the Intel Terminal. Ashley Williams or Kaidan Alenko can be found in the starboard observation deck while Garrus Vakarian can be found in the main battery. The medical officer, which can be either Dr. Chakwas or Dr. Chloe Michel, spends her time in the sick bay. The medical bay also has two terminals: one that can be used to purchase a reset of squad point allocations for the powers of Shepard and all other regular squad members (with the exception of Javik), and a second that can be used to purchase a reassignment of Shepard's bonus power to any other currently available option. EDI's mobile platform can sometimes be found in the AI Core, which is still accessible from inside the med bay just as it was in the previous game. Occasionally, characters may be located elsewhere on the deck; for example, Liara and Garrus may sometimes be found conversing in one of the lounges, and after Eve is brought on board, the Normandy's physician will temporarily relocate to the Crew Quarters. ##### Memorial Wall Located just outside the elevator there is a memorial wall featuring a record of crew casualties, including those who died on Prologue: Find the Beacon, Virmire, the Suicide Mission, and the twenty\-one crew members lost during the destruction of the Normandy SR\-1\. The wall will be updated throughout the game with the names of significant current or former crew members who die during the course of the story. On certain occasions, usually after significant events, different crew members can be found by the wall, gazing at it in contemplation. The ordering of names is not fixed, as they are placed in alphabetical order; when new names are added, some names previously on the wall will be in different positions. Richard L. Jenkins, the Virmire casualty (Kaidan Alenko or Ashley Williams), Charles Pressley, Abishek Pakti, Addison Chase, Alexei Dubyansky, Amina Waaberi, Carlton Tucks, Caroline Grenado, Germeen Barret, Harvey J. Gladstone, Hector Emerson, Helen M. Lowe, Jamin Bakari, Mandira Rahman, Marcus Grieco, Monica Negulesco, Orden Laflamme, Raymond Tanaka, Robert Felawa, Rosamund Draven, Silas Crosby, and Talitha Draven are always on the memorial wall from the start of Mass Effect 3\. Karin Chakwas, Kelly Chambers, Kenneth Donnelly, Gabriella Daniels, Rupert Gardner, Sarah Patel, Richard Hadley, Zach Matthews, Jenny Goldstein, Thomas Hawthorne, and Vadim Rolston will be on the wall if not rescued from the Collector Base. Any of the major members of Shepard's squad as well as Steve Cortez may end up with their name on the memorial wall by the epilogue of Mass Effect 3, depending on what choices Shepard made over the course of their mission. Their names will also be joined by David Anderson, and possibly the Commander as well. #### Deck 4: Engineering Deck 4 is the Engineering deck. It contains the Normandy's drive core; the starboard cargo room doubles as Diana Allers' quarters and her remote broadcast studio, while the port side cargo room serves as Javik's quarters. Tali and Engineer Adams work on the Engineering deck. If military pardons are issued through the Spectre Office in the Citadel Embassies, Adams will be joined by Kenneth Donnelly and Gabriella Daniels. #### Deck 5: Shuttle Bay Deck 5 is the Shuttle Bay. It contains the Normandy's armory, cargo hold, and two Kodiak shuttles. James Vega and Lieutenant Steve Cortez spend their time in the shuttle bay. Equipment from various retailers can also be purchased here via the procurement terminal at a slight premium over Citadel prices. A weapon modification bench and armor locker are also available here which Shepard can use to modify equipped weapons and armor respectively. A small gym is also found here, which James uses.

Lieutenant Steve Cortez was an Alliance pilot aboard the Normandy SR-2 in 2186, flying the UT-47A Kodiak that carried Commander Shepard and squad to missions, and a potential romance option for a male Shepard. An only child who lost both parents years earlier, Cortez had a husband, Robert, who was killed when the Collectors abducted the colony of Ferris Fields in 2185; Robert phoned Steve during the attack to tell him to escape and let him go. Steve kept a recording of the call and grieved heavily. He had served in the Alliance since around 2176, first in the First Fleet aboard the SSV Hawking flying F-61 Tridents, and five months before the Reaper invasion joined the Normandy SR-2 retrofit team, moving the armory to the shuttle bay.

Aboard the Normandy, Cortez maintained the armory alongside Lt. James Vega, an old friend from Fehl Prime, and preferred to keep busy to avoid thinking about Robert. Shepard could persuade him to take shore leave on the Citadel; he later visited the refugees' Memorial Wall to say goodbye to Robert and began to move on, reconnecting with old pilot friends and forwarding their information to Admiral Hackett to give the Alliance more pilots. A meeting at Purgatory could begin a relationship with a male Shepard or reinforce their friendship.

During the final assault on Earth, Cortez's shuttle was shot down by a Harvester after dropping off the squad. If he had visited the Memorial Wall he survived the crash and could be contacted by hologram; otherwise he died and Vega confirmed it, and his name appeared on the Normandy's memorial wall as "Steven Cortez." In the Leviathan DLC he crash-landed the shuttle and devised the plan for Shepard to reach Leviathan using a Triton mech. In the Citadel DLC he provided suppressive fire during the Spectre Archives infiltration, flew a skycar with Joker to block the hijacked Normandy from jumping to FTL, delivered a restrained Maya Brooks, and could take Shepard on a joyride in the Kodiak with the inertial dampeners disabled. If the Crucible was activated and the Reapers were controlled or Synthesis was chosen, Cortez placed Shepard's name on the memorial wall.

Besides being a Kodiak pilot aboard the Normandy SR\-2, Steve is also responsible for maintaining the Normandy's armory, a duty he shares with Lt. James Vega. Cortez and Vega are friends, having served together before on Fehl Prime. In between missions, they engage in off duty conversations. Cortez prefers to have as little time off from his duties as possible, since any time spent not working gives him too much time to think about Robert. Shepard has the option of convincing Cortez to take time off to leave the ship and succeeds. At first, Steve just loiters near the Normandy's docking bay on the Citadel, but he finds Shepard's suggestion a good idea since the vista of so many ships in flight brings him comfort and gets him thinking. He later visits the Memorial Wall for victims of Collector and Reaper attacks at the refugee docks, where Shepard can once more offer words of support. The downtime helps him to move on, and he meets up with some old pilot friends and forwards their information to Admiral Hackett, giving the Alliance some much needed pilots. A further encounter at Purgatory allows a male Shepard to begin a relationship with him, or reinforces their friendship otherwise. During the final assault on Earth, after dropping off Shepard's squad, Cortez's shuttle is shot down by a Harvester. If he has been persuaded to visit the Memorial Wall, he survives the crash and can be contacted via hologram later. Steve is later present in front of the Normandy's memorial wall with the rest of Shepard's surviving crew if the Crucible was activated, paying his respects to the dead. If Steve was never interacted with much, he dies when his shuttle gets shot during the final assault on Earth. He cannot be contacted and James confirms Cortez's death. Much later, if Shepard uses the Crucible, Steve's name is listed on the Normandy's memorial wall as "Steven Cortez".

- The anniversary of the First Contact War being called Armistice Day is similar to the November 11, 1918 signing of the armistice which effectively ended the First World War, which is commemorated in many Allied countries under several names, including Armistice Day, Remembrance Day, or Memorial Day. ##
If Gardner died at the Collector base, his name is added to the Normandy's Memorial Wall. If he survived, his current whereabouts are unknown.

Corporal Richard L. Jenkins was an Alliance Marine serving under Captain Anderson aboard the SSV Normandy. He was born in a rural district of Eden Prime and had dreamed of visiting more urban areas before enlisting, saying "even paradise gets boring." He wanted to prove himself as a notable soldier and test himself in combat, envied Commander Shepard's record, and admired the Spectres, being especially impressed by Nihlus Kryik after hearing that Nihlus once defeated an entire platoon single-handed, though his views were shaped more by vids than experience.

In Mass Effect, Jenkins was assigned to Shepard's ground team for the mission to Eden Prime and was killed by geth drones shortly after landing. His death was a blow to the morale of the Normandy's crew, who remembered him for his bold exuberance. Two years later, in Mass Effect 2, Doctor Chakwas recalled him during a drinking session with Shepard, telling how Jenkins was thrown back by a biotic display from Kaidan and, after Chakwas feared he had broken his back, jumped up shouting "That was awesome!" Chakwas cited Jenkins as one of the reasons she considered the Alliance great compared to Cerberus.

In 2186, the Normandy SR-2 received a memorial wall bearing the names of fallen crew from both the SR-2 and the SR-1, and Jenkins' name was included. If Shepard revisited Eden Prime, the Commander and some squadmates might briefly recall him and how he died on his birth world. Cut content from Mass Effect included a mess-hall scene, closely mirroring Chakwas' later story, in which Jenkins insists on Kaidan demonstrating his biotics and is tossed a cup before leaving disheartened for the cargo bay.

Mess Sergeant Rupert Gardner was an operative of Lazarus Cell and the cook and all-around handyman aboard the Normandy SR-2. He was one of the more openly pro-Cerberus crew members, telling Commander Shepard he was "damn proud" of the organization and dismissive of the Alliance and Council. Before joining Cerberus, Gardner had been a family man working element zero rigs along the frontier colonies until batarian raiders cost him everything; he then joined Cerberus to make a difference. He described himself as a jack-of-all-trades who handled any task that "falls through the cracks," including janitorial work and plumbing, and admitted he could not fight but was willing to help however he could.

Gardner asked Shepard to buy high-quality ingredients for the crew's meals, purchasable at the Zakera Cafe on the Citadel; if provided, crew members including Ken, Gabby, and Kasumi Goto commented on the improved food. He offered Shepard a calamari gumbo based on an asari recipe, joking that it seemed mildly cannibalistic for a tentacled race to eat squid but admitting the asari "know good grub."

If Shepard delayed traveling through the Omega 4 Relay after the crew's abduction, Gardner was processed into organic material with the rest of the crew; if the relay was used immediately, he could be saved along with Kelly Chambers and Dr. Chakwas. In Mass Effect 3, if he died at the Collector base his name was added to the Normandy's Memorial Wall; if he survived, his whereabouts were unknown. In an unimported Mass Effect 3 game his name appears on the memorial wall by default.

- The Normandy SR-1 led the assault that destroyed Sovereign at the Battle of the Citadel, and was later destroyed by a Collector cruiser near Alchera in 2183, killing over twenty crew including Navigator Charles Pressly; Cerberus built the larger Normandy SR-2 from her design (source: SSV Normandy)

- The Normandy SR-1 was named for the 1944 Allied invasion of Normandy, launched on its first mission to Eden Prime in 2183, played a critical supporting role at the Battle of the Citadel against Sovereign, and was destroyed above Alchera later that year by the Collectors, whose firepower far exceeded its design limits (source: The SSV Normandy SR-1 (Part 2) — Drive Core, Stealth, and Service History).
